summary: Solana Labs typosquat exfiltrates SSH keys, wallets, and credentials at install
details: This package impersonates Solana Labs (author field 'solana-labs', repository pointing at github.com/solana-labs/solana-web3) under an unrelated scope. Its postinstall.js runs automatically on npm install and, after a 1.5-3.5 second randomized delay, harvests installer-owned secrets: files under ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, Chrome/Firefox profile artifacts (Cookies, Login Data, key4.db), and cryptocurrency wallet directories (.bitcoin,.ethereum,.solana,.metamask,.exodus, and Electrum/Exodus AppData). It also iterates a hardcoded list of credential-shaped environment variables (NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, DOCKER_PASSWORD, GCLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN, MNEMONIC, SEED_PHRASE, multiple *_PRIVATE_KEY variables, and HELIUS/INFURA/ALCHEMY API keys). The collected profile is transmitted to two attacker-controlled destinations: the Telegram Bot API (bot 7231970337, chat_id 7231970337) via GET, and a serveo.net dynamic tunnel host at 40f955f39128bd79-178-249-214-24.serveousercontent.com via POST /collect. Variable identifiers in the script are masked (_jku, _wjn, _hyz, _ht, _tk, _ch) and the exfiltration is deferred behind a randomized timer to evade observation during install.
